correctness.rationale: For a period N orbit, T^q produces gcd(N,q) cycles of size N/gcd(N,q) and no smaller pairwise gap, proving the universal inequality including extended-real cases. The explicit rational Euclidean shells form a compact one-limit-point space, a homeomorphism rotates each shell, and direct coordinate comparisons give exact gaps epsilon_m and r_m/m. The resulting sequences qm epsilon_m^s and m^(1-s)/H_m^s have the claimed limits by harmonic estimates. The invariant small-diameter tail gives entropy zero. Exact-rational checker passed 420 diagnostics; finite checks are not the proof.

value.rationale: The source invariant is introduced to detect geometric packing of periodic cycles beyond entropy. The theorem establishes a general functorial one-sided law and an extreme failure of invariance under positive time iterates, already on a compact Euclidean planar homeomorphism with zero entropy and all nonfixed orbits finite. The exact endpoint critical-content value and fully explicit construction distinguish it from a bare qualitative counterexample, and identify a limitation relevant whenever the invariant is used to compare time discretizations.
